Vengeance
VEN-jens
noun (the LORD's prerogative of recompense)
From the Latin vindicare (to lay claim, avenge), through Old French vengeance; the just recompense of evil, which Scripture reserves to God and forbids to the individual.

See also: Vengeance

📖 Biblical Definition

Vengeance, in the biblical sense, is the just recompense of evil, a prerogative Scripture reserves to God and forbids to the private individual. The Lord declares it His own: “To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence”; and the apostle, citing this, commands believers, “Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.” The psalmist appeals to Him as the God to whom vengeance belongeth, and the writer to the Hebrews warns of falling into the hands of the God who has said, “Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense.” The dictionary holds two truths together that the modern mind struggles to keep. First, vengeance is real and righteous: God is just, He will by no means clear the guilty, and He will repay every wrong, either at the cross where the wrath fell on Christ for His people, or in the judgment where it falls on the impenitent. The cry of the martyrs under the altar, “How long, O Lord… dost thou not avenge our blood?” is heard and answered. Second, vengeance is God's, not ours: the believer is forbidden to repay evil for evil, commanded to love his enemies, and called to commit his cause to the righteous Judge. The dictionary marks the doctrine against the sentimentalism that denies God any vengeance at all, emptying His justice, and against the carnal heart that seizes vengeance for itself. To leave vengeance to God is not weakness but faith—the confidence that the Judge of all the earth will do right.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The just recompense of evil, a prerogative God reserves to Himself and forbids to the individual (Romans 12:19; Deuteronomy 32:35); real and righteous in God, forbidden as private revenge to men, who must commit their cause to the righteous Judge.

expand to see more

VENGEANCE, noun. [Latin vindicare, to avenge.] The just recompense of evil, belonging to God.

“To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence” (Deuteronomy 32:35).

“Avenge not yourselves… Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord” (Romans 12:19).

Real and righteous: God will repay every wrong, at the cross or in the judgment.

Forbidden to the individual, who must commit his cause to the righteous Judge.

📖 Key Scripture

Ro 12:19 — "Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord."

De 32:35 — "To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste."

Heb 10:30 — "For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people."

Ps 94:1 — "O LORD God, to whom vengeance belongeth; O God, to whom vengeance belongeth, shew thyself."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Sentimentalism denies God any vengeance at all, emptying His justice; the carnal heart seizes vengeance for itself, against the command to leave it to God.

expand to see more

The sentimental theology of the age cannot abide a God who avenges, and so it denies Him vengeance altogether, leaving a deity of indulgence who never repays evil. The dictionary names this a corruption of the divine justice. Scripture is emphatic: vengeance belongs to the LORD, who will repay; the same love that gave His Son to bear wrath for His people will pour out wrath on the impenitent who trample that Son under foot. A God incapable of vengeance is a God incapable of justice, and the blood of the martyrs cries to Him in vain. The doctrine of God's vengeance is the comfort of the oppressed and the terror of the oppressor.

The opposite corruption is as old as Cain: the carnal heart that seizes vengeance for itself, repaying evil for evil, nursing its grudges, and calling its retaliation justice. Against this Scripture is equally emphatic: avenge not yourselves; love your enemies; bless them that curse you; give place unto wrath. The dictionary holds the two truths together—that vengeance is real and righteous in God, and forbidden as a private possession to men. To renounce personal revenge is not to deny that justice will be done, but to entrust it to the One who alone can do it without sin: the righteous Judge who will by no means clear the guilty.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Latin vindicare (to lay claim, to avenge); the Hebrew naqam (to avenge) and the Greek ekdikesis (vengeance, vindication) name the recompense that belongs to God.

expand to see more

Naqam, Hebrew, to avenge or take vengeance, the LORD's prerogative.

Ekdikesis, Greek, vengeance or vindication, “vengeance is mine” (Romans 12:19).

Vindicare, Latin, to lay legal claim, to avenge, the root of “vengeance” and “vindicate.”

“Give place unto wrath” commits the matter to the wrath of God, not the hand of man.

The cry “how long… dost thou not avenge?” (Revelation 6:10) shows vengeance is heard and answered.

Usage

"The pastor comforted the wronged that vengeance belongs to the LORD, who will repay in His time."

"He rebuked the brother nursing revenge, for Scripture forbids us to avenge ourselves."

"She gave place unto wrath, entrusting her cause to the righteous Judge who cannot err."
